newsitem.title: USA: Best files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Best files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

text.p: Best Products Co. Inc. Tuesday filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, company officials and court documents said, marking the second time the retailer has sought bankruptcy protection in less than six years.
The company had previously filed for bankruptcy protection in January 1991 and emerged in June 1994.
It filed in U.S. bankruptcy court in Richmond, Virginia. The company said it obtained debtor-in-possession financing from CIT Group/Business Credit Inc in the amount of $250 million.

"The decision to file was a difficult one," said Daniel Levy, chairman and chief executive of the Richmond-based retailer. "... it was determined that the overall interests of our customers, vendors, associates and stockholders required immediate action be taken so normal operations may resume as expeditiously as is possible," he said.

Best Products, a speciality retailer offering assortments of jewelry and home furnishings, operates 169 Best stores in 23 states. The company also operates 11 Best Jewelry stores and a nationwide mail-order service.
"The commencement of the Chapter 11 was precipitated by Best Products' continuing sales decline and resulting deterioration of vendor support," Levy said.
Without adequate and balanced inventories for the important holiday season, Best Products would not realise the benefits of changes being implemented, Levy said.

Best Products had been considering all its alternatives, including the consideration of a proposed offer of merger made by Miami-based Ocean Reef Management, which was withdrawn, the company said in a statement.
"As the case goes forward, Best Products will continue to evaluate and take actions that will serve the best interests of all parties," Levy said.

Results for the second quarter filed in a notification of late filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month, showed a loss of $31.5 million, or $1.01 per share for the quarter ended Aug. 3. Sales were $268 million.
That compares with a net loss of $7.1 million, or 23 cents per share, on sales of $311.8 million in the same year-ago period.
For the six months the company's loss was $66.1 million, or $2.11 per share, compared with a loss of $15.2 million, or $0.48 per share, in the year earlier period.
Sales for the first half were $537.8 million vs. $584.6 million in the same year ago period.
